When a Texas School Police Officer Got ‘Riled Up’ Over a Defiant Teen
Over more than a year of reporting on school policing in Texas, I’ve read hundreds of police reports and talked to dozens of students. One case stood out.
In 2023, a 15-year-old was accused of pushing an assistant principal. When an officer confronted him, there was a scuffle and the boy was tackled and handcuffed.
The encounter moved inside the school police office, where the officer rammed his fists into the teen’s belly, berated him and slapped him on the side of the head.
The student was charged with assault and resisting arrest. The assault charge was later reduced to making a threat, court records show.
This case underscores concerns raised by parents about law enforcement on campus: that officers might clash with students and derail their lives.
